claims.statement: The watchlist membership association `market_watchlists_securities` is an entity rather than a bare join table: it has a composite primary key over `watchlist_id`/`security_id`, carries `added_at` and an application-managed `position`, and both foreign keys use `ondelete="CASCADE"`, while `market_watchlists` carries the persisted `sort` column and a unique `(user_id, name)` constraint.

The watchlist sort/membership migration `4c2ed77e7738` adds `market_watchlists.sort`, `market_watchlists_securities.added_at` and `position` as nullable columns with server defaults, backfills them deterministically (`row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY watchlist_id ORDER BY security_id)`, `sort` to `custom`), and only then enforces `NOT NULL` — the worked example of the model-change-plus-revision rule.

`WatchlistRepository` is an ABC declaring twelve operations that the router resolves with `services.aget(WatchlistRepository)` and calls directly; there is no backend watchlist service, and only `create_default` has no route.

Every watchlist operation is scoped to the owning `user_id` through the single ownership gate `_get_owned`, which raises `WatchlistNotFoundError` for a missing or foreign watchlist so the two cases are deliberately indistinguishable, and the global `EntityNotFoundError` handler in `src/main.py` turns it into a 404 with an `{"error": ...}` body.

`WatchlistDuplicateNameError` and `WatchlistOrderIdentityError` are deliberately plain `Exception` subclasses rather than `EntityNotFoundError` subclasses, so the global 404 handler cannot claim them; the create/update routes translate the first to HTTP 409 and the reorder route translates the second to HTTP 422.

An invalid `sort` value never reaches the repository: `WatchlistSortMode` is a `StrEnum` used as the Pydantic field type of `WatchlistUpdate.sort`, so an unknown value is a FastAPI 422 validation error and nothing is stored.

`set_security_order` validates that the payload is an exact permutation of the current membership before any write — the length check catches a repeated id because `set` collapses duplicates — so a rejected payload raises `WatchlistOrderIdentityError` with every stored position untouched; a payload equal to the current order is a no-op and `[]` is the valid permutation of an empty watchlist.

Membership `position` is application-managed: a non-existing membership is inserted with `max(position) + 1` as a scalar subquery (appending in add order, explicitly not concurrency-safe), `added_at` is stamped with `func.now()`, re-adding an existing membership is idempotent, and the watchlist is reloaded with `populate_existing=True` because the explicit association insert leaves the in-session collection stale.

The default watchlist is the one literally named `"Default"` — there is no `is_default` column. The id-less shortcut routes depend on that name lookup: `add_security` creates the list on first add (tolerating a concurrent-create `IntegrityError` by rolling back and re-reading) and `remove_security` raises `WatchlistNotFoundError` with the nil UUID when no `"Default"` list exists.

`market_update_watchlist` applies `rename` when `payload.name` is set and `update_sort` when `payload.sort` is set (so a combined payload does both), and when neither is set it still proves ownership by re-reading the user's watchlists and raising `WatchlistNotFoundError` for an absent id — an empty `PATCH {}` returns the current watchlist instead of silently succeeding on a foreign id.

Watchlist reads are price-enriched per response rather than per security: `_fetch_price_metrics` issues one `row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY security_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC)` query keeping the latest two closes, and `_enrich_watchlists` unions the security ids of all watchlists so `GET /watchlists` costs exactly one metrics query regardless of list or membership count.

The enrichment metric semantics are: no closes leaves the three fields `None`; exactly one close sets `current_price` and leaves both change fields `None`; two or more closes set `current_price` to the latest close, `daily_price_change` to the difference against the previous close, and `daily_price_change_percent` to that difference over the previous close times 100 — or `None` when the previous close is `0`.

`WatchlistRead` carries `sort` and embeds `WatchlistSecuritySchema` items, which extend `SecuritySchema` with the membership `added_at` (typed `AwareDatetime`, so a naive timestamp fails validation on the way out) and `position`.

The watchlist ordering split: the stored membership `position` is authoritative for manual order and is what the embedded reads order by (with `added_at` as tiebreaker), the paginated `get_securities` route instead pages by `symbol`, and the persisted `WatchlistSortMode` is a client-applied preference that `update_sort` stores but the repository never orders by.

`WatchlistService` (a Svelte 5 runes class) is the single client-side owner of watchlist state: `+layout.svelte` calls `setWatchlistService()` once and `setContext`s the instance, consumers read it through `getWatchlistService()`, and the module never exports a module-level instance, so SSR cannot bleed one request's watchlists into another's.

The root layout owns the single initial watchlist load in a `$effect` gated on `data.user` (never run during SSR): it awaits `loadWatchlists()`, routes a returned error through `redirectOn401`, and then warms `/portfolios`, `/watchlists`, `/holdings` and the first ten default-watchlist `/security/{id}` targets fire-and-forget, each URL prefetched at most once via a per-instance `SvelteSet` with rejected prefetches swallowed.

`/watchlists` deliberately does not duplicate the layout's fetch: its `+page.server.ts` returns `{ watchlists: [] }` with no request so the shell paints instantly, and the page only seeds `watchlistService.watchlists` from `data.watchlists` when the service array is still empty — a guard that is inert while the server load stays empty.

`WatchlistService` write behaviour: every mutator clears `this.error` first; `replaceWatchlist` swaps exactly one element by id so an operation on one list never clobbers another; `reorderSecurities` is the only optimistic write (it rebuilds the target's securities in the caller's id order, rewriting each `position` to its index, before awaiting the PUT, then replaces with the server payload); and `removeSecurityFromWatchlist`, `reorderSecurities` and `toggleSecurity` call `loadWatchlists` to resync *before* recording the error, because the resync clears the shared error at its start.
`setSort` is explicitly not optimistic: the PATCH response already carries both the new `sort` and the backend-ordered securities, so there is nothing to pre-apply locally.

`WatchlistService.addSecurity(watchlistId, result, token)` is the resolve-or-create orchestration: it returns immediately with no network call when the target list already holds the same `symbol` + `exchange` case-insensitively, otherwise reuses the `id` of a matching security found in any loaded watchlist, and only as a last resort calls `createOrUpdateSecurity({ code, exchange, name, currency: 'USD' })` before adding membership and replacing the returned list.

`hasSecurity` and `toggleSecurity` operate on the default watchlist only (`hasSecurity` inspects `defaultWatchlistSecurities`), so the star toggle works without a watchlist id by calling the id-less `removeFromWatchlist`/`addToWatchlist` routes.

The sidebar renders one collapsible group per watchlist, ordered by `sortWatchlistsByOrder(watchlists, watchlistOrder)` where `watchlistOrder` comes from the `initialWatchlistOrder` context or `$page.data.watchlist_order`; the helper sorts the ids present in the order array by index and appends any watchlist missing from it in original relative order, so a newly created list never disappears.

Sidebar collapse state lives in a `SvelteSet<string>` seeded from the `initialCollapsedWatchlistIds` context or `$page.data.collapsed_watchlist_ids`, and `toggleCollapsed` persists the whole array with a fire-and-forget `patchPreferences({ collapsed_watchlist_ids })`; the `1`–`9`/`0` ticker hints are passed only for the default watchlist's securities, and a security-less group renders a muted `No securities` row.

The layout's document-level `handleKeydown` returns early when a modifier is held or the event target is an `INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT` or `contenteditable` element; it owns `/` (toggle global search), `p`, `w` and `h`, and for a bare digit computes `index = e.key === '0' ? 9 : Number(e.key) - 1`, reads `watchlistService.defaultWatchlistSecurities[index]`, prefetches and `goto`s `/security/{id}`.

The `/watchlists` page offers exactly six sort options in order (`Custom`, `Name (alphabetical)`, `Price Change (Gainers)`, `Price Change (Losers)`, `Date added (newest first)`, `Date added (oldest first)`) each with a visual direction used for the active option's chevron, calls `watchlistService.setSort` on select, supports inline rename where Enter commits and a recorded error keeps the editor open, and its `+` button opens the layout's global search pre-targeted via the `openGlobalSearch(watchlist)` context callback.

`normalizeWatchlistSort` narrows an unknown, `null` or absent key to `'custom'` against the `WATCHLIST_SORT_KEYS` list, and `sortSecurities` implements each mode over the membership metadata (`custom` by `position`, `name_asc`/`name_desc` by `localeCompare`, `price_change_desc`/`price_change_asc` by `daily_price_change_percent` with `null`s last, `date_added`/`date_added_asc` by comparing `added_at`), falling through to `position` order for anything unrecognised; `name_desc` is unreachable through the persisted contract because it is absent from both the `WatchlistSort` union and `WATCHLIST_SORT_KEYS`.

Watchlist rows render on the shared static `WATCHLIST_ROW_DATA_TRACKS` Tailwind literal so every row has identical column tracks, with the Added cell always rendered (a dash when `added_at` is missing or unparseable) to preserve later track offsets; display formatting comes from `watchlist-utils.ts` (`formatPrice`, `formatPriceChangePercent`, `formatDateAdded` in deterministic `en-US`/UTC, `formatValuationRange`), and the Valuation column is filled by one `getValuationsBatch` call whose rejection is non-fatal and falls back to `—`.

The `/watchlists` page has two independent reorder modes: watchlist-level order (`Reorder`/`Done`) persists to the user preference, not to the watchlists — `moveWatchlist` snapshots `watchlistOrder` and the service array, applies the move optimistically, announces the new position into a polite live region, persists `watchlist_order` via `patchPreferences`, and on rejection restores both snapshots and sets `watchlistService.error` — while security-level order is offered per watchlist only when that list's persisted sort is `custom` and is disabled while watchlist reorder mode is active.

Keyboard reordering goes through the shared `handleReorderKeydown`, which always `preventDefault`s ArrowUp/ArrowDown so the page does not scroll and is a no-op past either end, and `restoreHandleFocus(handle)` re-focuses the grab handle after `tick()` only when the keyed `{#each}` reconciliation actually dropped focus to `<body>` — never stealing it from a control the user has since moved to.

The global-search dialog searches through a 300 ms `debounce` wrapper over `marketService.search(query)` driven by an `$effect` on `query`, clears results without a request for an empty query, groups the flat results into `Record<security_type, results>` defaulting the key to `'other'` when empty, and sets `shouldFilter={false}` on the command dialog because the server already searched.

The search endpoint `GET /market/search` (aliased at `/market/securities/search`) constrains `q` to 1–100 characters, reads `SecuritySearchCache` first and only calls the market gateway on a miss, writing the cache once; the cache key is the normalized (trimmed, lowercased, whitespace-collapsed) query with a default TTL of 30 days (`DEFAULT_SEARCH_CACHE_TTL = 2_592_000`).

The global-search star is target-aware: `activeTargetWatchlist` re-resolves the bound `targetWatchlist` against the service's current `watchlists` (falling back to the bound object) so the dialog reflects live state after a toggle, the placeholder switches between `Search securities to add to {name}...` and the generic prompt, and `handleWatchlistToggle` removes the existing membership from the target list or resolves-then-adds, falling back to the default-list `toggleSecurity` path when no target is bound.

Selecting a global-search result calls `createOrUpdateSecurity`, closes the dialog and `goto`s `/security/{id}`, and a second `$effect` resets `query`, `searchResults` and `targetWatchlist` whenever the dialog is closed so reopening never shows the previous session's results or target.

The watchlist router and repository test suites run against an ephemeral testcontainers PostgreSQL (or a `TEST_DATABASE_URL` override) rather than external services, pinning duplicate-name rejection with a usable session after rollback, ownership scoping, cascade deletes, append-order positions with tz-aware `added_at`, the four rejected order payloads leaving positions unchanged, and the price-enrichment matrix; the frontend suites mock the API clients instead.
